visuals: The red sand and sparse yellow grass of the Kalahari Desert in South Africa under a bright sun.
script: From the sandy Kalahari desert.

visuals: The dramatic, wild cliffs of the South African coast with waves crashing against the rocks.
script: To grassy plains and wild cliffs, the land here is pure adventure. It is like nature couldn't decide, so it picked everything!

visuals: Table Mountain in Cape Town, South Africa, with its iconic flat top and a cable car ascending toward the summit above the city.
script:
And get this: there’s Table Mountain in Cape Town. It’s a big flat mountain known for its unique shape and amazing views. 
You can ride a cable car with spinning views all the way to the top. Who wouldn’t want that?

visuals: A graceful springbok leaping through the tall golden grass of a South African savanna.
script: But the real "superhero" of the wild is our national animal, the springy springbok! It is so speedy that even the national rugby team is named after it.

visuals: A rare, scaly pangolin walking through the dry grass of a South African nature reserve.
script: Oh, and let’s not forget the pangolin: shy, scaly, and protected across Africa, including in South Africa. This rare little guy is like a walking artichoke.

visuals: A powerful rhinoceros standing in a grassy field in Kruger National Park, South Africa, with mountains in the distance.
script: One more wild fact: South Africa shines with wildlife in Kruger National Park. Ever seen a rhino up close?

visuals: A collection of raw gold nuggets and sparkling uncut diamonds displayed on a dark surface.
script: And South Africa shines with gold and diamonds.

visuals: The Union Buildings in Pretoria, South Africa, surrounded by blooming purple jacaranda trees in spring.
script: Ready for the capital? Trick question… There are THREE! Pretoria is where the president works: it’s bursting with purple jacaranda trees in spring.

visuals: The historic Houses of Parliament building in Cape Town, South Africa, under a clear blue sky.
script: This is where laws are made and debates happen. Cape Town is the legislative heart of South Africa, shaping the rules that everyone follows.

visuals: The grand Supreme Court of Appeal building in Bloemfontein, South Africa, with its historic architecture.
script: and Bloemfontein handles the courts. Triple the capitals, triple the fun!

visuals: The modern Johannesburg skyline in South Africa at sunset, with its tall buildings glowing with a golden light.
script: Johannesburg is the biggest city! It boomed after gold was discovered in 1886 and still sparkles today.

visuals: A group of small African penguins waddling on the white sands of Boulders Beach in South Africa, near large granite boulders.
script: Just a few hours away, Cape Town shows a totally different side: Boulders Beach is home to tuxedo-wearing African penguins, waddling around like it’s party time!

visuals: A quiet, historic street in the Bo-Kaap neighborhood of Cape Town, South Africa, with its brightly colored houses and cobblestone paths.
script: Wanna hear something really cool? South Africa has 11 official languages! Zulu and Xhosa are the most widely spoken. That’s a whole lotta chatting!

visuals: A pleasant afternoon at the Moses Mabhida Stadium in Durban, South Africa, with pedestrians walking near the iconic arch and modern walkways.
script: About 60 million people call this place home, that’s around as many as in California. Imagine a stadium that big… whoa!

visuals: A traditional South African bobotie dish (spiced minced meat) with a golden egg-based topping, served with yellow rice.
script: And now… FOOD TIME! How about bobotie? It’s a baked meat dish with curry spices, topped with a golden egg custard. Yum!

visuals: A wooden bowl filled with strips of traditional South African biltong (spiced dried meat).
script: Snack attack? Grab some biltong! Spiced dried meat, like supercharged jerky.

visuals: A cup of warm, red-brown South African rooibos tea served on a wooden table near a bunch of fresh rooibos plant branches.
script: And wash it all down with rooibos, a smooth red tea that’s naturally caffeine-free and enjoyed all over South Africa.

visuals: South African gumboot dancers in black boots and traditional work clothes performing a rhythmic stomp on an outdoor stage.
script: Now for my favorite part: music and dance! Gumboot dancing started in South African mines as a way for workers to communicate without speaking. Today, it’s an upbeat tradition full of stomps, slaps, and smiles.

visuals: A joyful Heritage Day celebration in South Africa with people in diverse traditional outfits, drumming and sharing food.
script: Don’t miss Heritage Day either! Music, food, and clothes bursting with color!

visuals: Cheering South African fans in a stadium during the 2010 World Cup, blowing colorful vuvuzelas and waving the national flag.
script: In 1994, South Africa became a democracy. That was huge. And in 2010, it made history again by hosting the first-ever men’s World Cup held in Africa. Remember all those LOUD vuvuzelas? BZZZZZZZ!

visuals: A portrait of Nelson Mandela smiling and wearing a South African national rugby jersey.
script: Nelson Mandela, the peacemaker legend, believed sports could unite a whole nation. Pretty awesome, right?

visuals: South African runner Caster Semenya racing on a professional track in her national team uniform.
script: Caster Semenya, a super fast runner, made her mark by grabbing gold in the 800 meters at the 2012 London Games.
